title: A 74W/48V Monolithic-GaN Integrated Adjustable Multilevel Supply Modulator for 5G Base-Station Massive-MIMO Arrays
problem: 5G and 6G base-station transmitters require efficient power management for RF power amplifiers in massive-MIMO arrays. Analog envelope tracking (AET) has limitations in bandwidth, modulation complexity, and high-voltage applications. Digital envelope tracking (DET) separates voltage generation (slow, efficient) and tracking (fast) stages but conventional architectures lack efficient multilevel voltage generation.
method: Monolithic GaN-based adjustable multilevel supply modulator implementing digital envelope tracking architecture. Separates voltage generation (VG) stage producing multiple voltage levels efficiently at slow rates, and tracker (TR) stage for fast voltage adjustment. Multilevel architecture reduces voltage ripple and losses vs. binary switching. 48V operation at 74W power delivery for base-station class PA supply. GaN integration achieves high efficiency and thermal performance on single die.

title: Using Analytical Performance/Power Model and Fine-Grained DVFS to Enhance AI Accelerator Energy Efficiency
problem: DVFS on AI processors has historically been applied at coarse granularity (entire program or sub-phases) because the control latency of DVFS mechanisms exceeds the duration of individual AI operators, leaving per-operator energy optimization unexploited. This coarse-grained DVFS fails to match voltage/frequency to the actual compute intensity of each AI operator.
method: The paper proposes an analytical performance/power model that characterizes the compute- and memory-boundedness of individual AI operators, enabling prediction of which operators tolerate voltage/frequency reduction without performance loss. Combined with a hardware mechanism to reduce DVFS control latency, the system applies fine-grained DVFS at the AI-operator level: memory-bound operators run at lower frequency while compute-bound operators run at peak frequency, minimizing energy waste during memory-stall phases.

title: DuQTTA: Dual Quantized Tensor-Train Adaptation with Decoupling Magnitude-Direction for Efficient Fine-Tuning of LLMs
problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for LLMs struggle to balance accuracy and efficiency at scale, particularly when targeting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices with severe memory and compute limitations.
method: DuQTTA combines Tensor-Train decomposition with dual-stage quantization and adaptive optimization strategy with decoupled magnitude-direction updates to minimize model size, achieving up to 65x compression on LLaMA2-7B while improving over LoRA through architectural co-design for edge deployment.

title: Delinquent Loop Pre-execution Using Predicated Helper Threads
problem: Helper-thread branch pre-execution fails when delinquent branches are control-dependent on other delinquent branches: prior work must branch-predict the first delinquent branch (b1) in the helper thread to decide whether to pre-execute the second (b2), merely shifting the misprediction bottleneck to the helper thread. Additionally, stores that both influence a delinquent branch and are control-dependent on it create a disambiguation problem in helper threads.
method: Phelps (Predicated Helper Threads) constructs a helper thread for each inner loop containing delinquent branches and unconditionally pre-executes all delinquent branches (including control-dependent ones) in every loop iteration. Per-branch queues are managed in lockstep with loop iterations, so the main thread can correctly consume or ignore b2 outcomes based on b1 results. Influential stores that are control-dependent on delinquent branches are predicated on those branch outcomes in the helper thread. A dual decoupled helper thread scheme handles outer-inner loop pairs with short/unpredictable inner-loop trip counts.

title: Gaze into the Pattern: Characterizing Spatial Patterns with Internal Temporal Correlations for Hardware Prefetching
problem: Existing spatial-region hardware prefetchers predict memory access footprints using system-level context features (trigger PC, data address) that fail to capture the intrinsic characteristics of spatial access patterns, resulting in poor flexibility and suboptimal prefetch accuracy across diverse workloads.
method: Gaze extracts footprint-internal temporal correlations — the ordering and timing relationships among cache line accesses within a spatial region — as the primary feature for characterizing and predicting spatial access patterns. This avoids dependence on trigger PC or address-based context lookup. For spatial streaming patterns (very high access density within a region), Gaze applies a dedicated two-stage prefetch approach to suppress over-prefetching: a first stage filters high-density streaming footprints and a second stage applies targeted prefetch decisions to avoid redundant prefetches.

title: In-Storage Acceleration of Retrieval Augmented Generation as a Service
problem: As RAG deployments shift knowledge bases to persistent NVMe storage to handle ever-growing corpora, the Search & Retrieval phase — comprising embedding model inference, similarity/relevance search over dynamic data structures, and long-latency storage accesses — becomes the dominant bottleneck for end-to-end latency.
method: The paper proposes a metamorphic in-storage accelerator architecture embedded within NVMe storage devices. The in-storage accelerator is programmable to support diverse RAG retrieval algorithms, dynamic data structures (e.g., HNSW, IVF), and varying computational patterns. It executes smaller language models for query embedding generation entirely in-storage, while the final LLM generation runs on DGX A100 systems. The metamorphic design adapts its functional units to the retrieval algorithm at hand without requiring host CPU involvement in the hot path.

title: ATLAS: A Self-Supervised and Cross-Stage Netlist Power Model for Fine-Grained Time-Based Layout Power Analysis
problem: Accurate power prediction for new designs requires time-consuming back-end processing and commercial tool simulation; delays design optimization cycles and prevents rapid power-driven exploration.
method: ATLAS employs pre-training and fine-tuning paradigm customized for circuit power. Uses self-supervised learning to predict ultimate layout-stage power from gate-level netlist without layout information. Targets golden per-cycle power from commercial simulation tools, handling separate prediction for clock tree, registers, and combinational logic.

title: Truly Pre-Routing Timing Prediction via Considering Power Delivery Network
problem: Pre-routing timing prediction in chip design ignores power delivery network (PDN) effects, leading to inaccurate timing predictions. Existing ML-assisted methods fail to capture IR drop and routing congestion impacts on timing.
method: Proposes two specialized encoders—an IR drop-aware encoder and routing congestion-aware encoder—that fuse multimodal data (netlist, layout, PDN) through Pareto optimization to balance utilization across modalities for improved timing prediction accuracy on TSMC 16nm designs.

title: CAE-DFKD: Bridging the Transferability Gap in Data-Free Knowledge Distillation
problem: Existing data-free knowledge distillation (DFKD) methods focus on image-level recognition performance without addressing transferability of learned representations to downstream tasks.
method: Proposes Category-Aware Embedding DFKD (CAE-DFKD) that operates at the embedding level rather than image level; alters generator training paradigm to improve representation quality and downstream task transfer.

title: 34.3 A 4.75GHz Digital PLL with 45.8fs Integrated-Jitter and 257dB FoM Based on a Voltage-Biased Harmonic-Shaping DCO with Adaptive Common-Mode Resonance Tuning
problem: Digital PLLs for low-jitter synthesis must minimize DCO flicker and white noise, but voltage-biased DCOs require complex tuning-bank segmentation and extensive manual common-mode (CM) resonance tuning that is PVT-sensitive.
method: A voltage-biased DCO with harmonic-shaping architecture employs adaptive common-mode resonance tuning based on second-harmonic amplitude, enabling automatic foreground/background tuning across PVT variations. The approach uses wideband CM resonance expansion via transformer to maintain high CM impedance across the full tuning range.

title: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
problem: Prevalent LLM quantization methods (W8A8 or W4-only) do not fully utilize INT4 tensor cores on modern GPUs and cannot reduce the KV cache memory bottleneck, because quantizing activations to 4-bit causes unacceptable accuracy loss with standard methods, leaving W4A4 impractical.
method: COMET introduces a fine-grained mixed-precision quantization algorithm (FMPQ) that compresses most activations to 4-bit while preserving accuracy by identifying and retaining outlier activations at higher precision (e.g., 8-bit) in a mixed-precision format. On the hardware side, COMET develops a highly optimized W4Ax GPU kernel (supporting both W4A4 and W4A8 mixed-precision GEMM) with a novel mixed-precision data layout that co-locates 4-bit and 8-bit activation elements to enable fast dequantization. The kernel uses GPU software pipelining to overlap data loading and conversion with computation, and introduces fine-grained streaming multiprocessor (SM) scheduling to achieve load balance across SMs. COMET integrates this kernel into a full LLM inference framework with efficient KV4 cache management supporting models like LLaMA-3-70B on a single A100-80G.

title: EPICS: Efficient Parallel Pattern Fault Simulation for Sequential Circuits via Strongly Connected Components
problem: Gate-level fault simulation for large sequential circuits is time-consuming; existing parallel-pattern techniques fail for sequential circuits due to timing dependencies within feedback loops (strongly connected components).
method: EPICS combines loop fusion (compiling simple loops into larger nodes) with event-driven simulation; selects loop entrance nodes via indegree analysis for larger SCCs; implements lazy propagation for internal nodes; strategically mixes compiled and event-driven modes.

title: Enhancing Large-Scale AI Training Efficiency: The C4 Solution for Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Communication Optimization
problem: Large-scale distributed LLM training across thousands of GPUs suffers from efficiency loss due to (1) hardware failures that are slow to detect and isolate, and (2) network traffic collisions that cause prolonged GPU idle time during collective communication synchronization steps.
method: C4 exploits two properties of distributed training workloads: (1) homogeneous, iteration-structured load means hardware anomalies produce detectable syndromes in collective communication patterns, enabling rapid faulty-component identification, isolation, and task restart without waiting for software-level timeouts; (2) collective communication involves a small number of long-lived, predictable flows, allowing C4 to perform proactive traffic planning that eliminates bandwidth contention among these flows and reduces collision-induced queuing.

title: Identifying System-on-Chip Security Assets with Structure-Based Analysis
problem: SoC designs integrate components from multiple sources, creating complex attack surfaces; identifying and protecting security assets (cryptographic keys, sensitive data, control logic) is critical but currently manual and time-intensive, slowing security validation and risk assessment.
method: Automated framework for SoC security asset identification: transforms RTL code into graph representations, applies deep neural networks (DNNs) to classify nodes as security or non-security assets based on structural patterns learned from training data. Graph representation captures connectivity and data flow information.

title: A Full-system, Programmable, and Extensible In-Memory Computing Simulation Framework for Deep Learning
problem: Designing scalable, programmable IMC platforms for modern generative AI (LLMs, DiTs) lacks simulation infrastructure that accurately models device-level physics while supporting full-stack software integration.
method: IMCsim provides full-system simulation: (1) ISA extensions for tensor operations, (2) mappable to eNVM-, SRAM-, or digital IMC architectures, (3) validated against silicon prototypes (22nm MRAM, 28nm SRAM), (4) enables PPA trade-off exploration across workloads.

title: TidalMesh: Topology-Driven AllReduce Collective Communication for Mesh Topology
problem: Existing AllReduce algorithms are topology-aware adaptations of generic algorithms (ring, tree) to physical 2D mesh networks, resulting in a mismatch between logical and physical communication patterns that wastes bandwidth and increases latency.
method: TidalMesh is a topology-driven AllReduce algorithm designed natively for 2D mesh networks. It pushes data flows between endpoint nodes in a wave-like (tidal) pattern that aligns with the mesh grid structure, fully utilizing bidirectional links and minimizing congestion. Sparse TidalMesh minimizes the bandwidth overhead of the base algorithm. Collective communication unrolling enables software pipelining by superimposing different AllReduce phases (ReduceScatter, AllGather) so that compute and communication overlap across multiple concurrent AllReduce operations, effectively hiding collective communication latency.
